# Chapter 9: Common Design Patterns — 9.9–9.11

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), and CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest. Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 9.9 Template Method

- **FDG9124** AVOID making public members virtual. (library only) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9124
- **FDG9125** CONSIDER using the Template Method Pattern to provide more controlled extensibility. (library only) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9125
- **FDG9126** CONSIDER naming protected virtual members that provide extensibility points for nonvirtual members by suffixing the nonvirtual member name with “Core.” (library only) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9126
- **FDG9127** DO perform argument and state validation in the nonvirtual member of the Template Method Pattern before calling the virtual member. (not in test projects)
- **FDG9128** DO only perform argument and state validation unique to the derived type in the virtual member of the Template Method Pattern. That is, do not repeat validation from the nonvirtual member. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9128

## 9.10 Timeouts

- **FDG9129** DO prefer method parameters as the mechanism for users to provide timeout time. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9129
- **FDG9131** DO throw `System.TimeoutException` when a timeout elapses. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9131
- **FDG9132** DO NOT return error codes to indicate timeout expiration. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9132

## 9.11 XAML Readable Types

- **FDG9133** CONSIDER providing the default constructor if you want a type to work with XAML. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9133
- **FDG9134** DO provide markup extension if you want an immutable type to work with XAML readers. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9134
- **FDG9135** AVOID defining new type converters unless the conversion is natural and intuitive. In general, limit type converter usage to the ones already provided by .NET. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9135
- **FDG9136** CONSIDER applying the `ContentPropertyAttribute` to enable convenient XAML syntax for the most commonly used property. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9136
